html:
The Ashtadhyayi, "eight chapters", is a grammar of Sanskrit written by Panini, probably in the 5th or 4th century BCE. It is the oldest complete grammar of any language and one of the most exact ever written.

Panini came from Shalatura in Gandhara, near today's Attock in Pakistan. Almost nothing else is known about him.

The work describes the whole language in just under 4,000 short rules. The rules are written in a code of Panini's own: markers, abbreviations and rules about rules, applied in a fixed order. Starting from roots and endings, the rules produce every correct Sanskrit word and sentence. It was made to be learnt by heart and spoken, and may have been composed without writing.

Its effects:

  • It fixed Sanskrit. The language of Kalidasa a thousand years later follows Panini's rules.
  • European scholars met it around 1800. It shaped the new science of linguistics, including the ideas of the root and the sound unit.
  • Its rule system is often compared to the notation later invented to describe computer languages.
sum: The Ashtadhyayi, "eight chapters", is a grammar of Sanskrit written by Panini, probably in the 5th or 4th century BCE. It is the oldest complete grammar of any language and one of the most exact ever written.
